title: Predictive warm-pool and cross-region shadowing for connection resilience (Redis/Kafka/DB)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: reduce tail latency and improve availability during cross-region and downstream store perturbations by combining workload forecasting, token-aware warm connection pools, and non-blocking shadowing to secondary replicas. This ticket prototypes a predictive warm-pool controller that: 1) forecasts short-term QPS and sequence length distribution at the tenant/route level; 2) pre-warms connections and warmed KV caches for Redis and DB replicas; 3) sends probabilistic shadow copies to secondary region replicas for fast cold-start failover; 4) integrates with circuit-breaker thresholds and progressive load-shedding policies to preserve SLOs. The approach emphasizes minimal synchronous overhead on the critical path and observable SLO-driven trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end prototype deploys in staging across two regions and can pre-warm 80% of expected connections within the forecast window
Latency tail (P99) for small seq-length requests decreases by >=15% in cold-cache scenarios compared to baseline
Failover time to secondary region under simulated outage is <= 300ms with no client-perceived errors for read-only flows
Circuit-breaker integration triggers soft-shed tiers and prevents >5% sustained SLO violations during 5-minute downstream saturation tests
Comprehensive dashboards and runbook links are added; playbook tested with chaos run and postmortem created
comments: 2026-02-22 - Spike complete: implemented simple ARIMA-based qps forecaster + token-aware weight. Initial results: good hit rate for 60s horizon in steady traffic (85% correct warm decisions). - Lina

2026-03-01 - Design review (PM/Infra): agreed to keep shadowing probabilistic (10% default) to avoid write amplification and to only shadow read-only replica queries. Action: add per-customer opt-out. - Marco (PM)

2026-03-04 - Engineering note: multiplexing layer needed minor API change to expose warm-state hints to runtime; opened GH PR #redwood/runtime-connpool PR-479 (see links). Implementation uses non-blocking optimistic acquisition to avoid head-of-line stalls.

2026-03-07 - Load test 1: saturating Redis with synthetic tenant mix; discovered connection storm when forecast overshoots during ramp. Mitigation: add dampening factor and conservative upper bound tied to token-bank budget. Created follow-up task ENG-902342.

2026-03-10 - Integration with circuit breakers: threshold values tuned to 75th percentile CPU and 2x median latency. In practice we saw earlier tripping prevents cache thrash. Need SRE validation for production thresholds. - Lina
2026-03-12 - PM review: approved staging rollout with 5% traffic canary and observability checks gating promotion. Documented playbook in Confluence and attached runbook. - Aisha
investigation_findings: Warm pool hit-rate correlates strongly with short-term qps autocorrelation; tenants with low autocorrelation (bursty) require larger safety margins
Probabilistic shadowing reduces cold-failover latency but increases upstream network egress and read load on secondary replicas; limit to read-only flows and set per-tenant caps
Token-aware admission prevents single noisy-tenant pre-warm storms by enforcing per-tenant warm budget and priority lanes
